title: Pixel-art stone brick wall with bevels and moss
purpose: Generate a tileable pixel-art brick or stone-block wall at a chosen art resolution: staggered courses, one-pixel mortar, light and shadow bevels on every brick, grain, cracks and moss, with per-pixel normal, height, roughness and occlusion maps. Use for castle, dungeon and town walls in 2D games.

contract.signature: generate(width=256, height=256, seed=0, preset="default", directx_normal=False, **parameters) -> {map name: {"channels", "colour_space", "pixels"}}
contract.command_line: python pixel_stone_bricks.py --size 1024 --seed 7 --preset NAME --out DIR [--width W --height H] [--set NAME=VALUE] [--directx-normal] [--orm]

parameters.name: art_pixels
parameters.meaning: Art pixels along each side of the tile; the maps enlarge them with nearest-neighbour sampling.

parameters.name: courses
parameters.meaning: Brick courses across the tile height.

parameters.name: bricks_per_course
parameters.meaning: Bricks in each course across the tile width.

parameters.name: irregularity
parameters.meaning: Random variation of brick lengths and course offsets (0 is a regular running bond).

parameters.name: cracks
parameters.meaning: Share of bricks with a crack.

parameters.name: relief
parameters.meaning: Strength of the per-pixel normal map.

parameters.name: hue_shift
parameters.meaning: Hue rotation of the albedo in turns.

presets.name: default
presets.description: Grey castle stone in staggered courses with a little moss.

presets.name: sandstone
presets.description: Warm sandstone blocks, three courses, crisp and clean.

presets.name: mossy_ruin
presets.description: Old green-grey ruin stones, cracked and overgrown.

presets.name: red_brick
presets.description: Small red bricks in a regular running bond with pale mortar.

limits: Stylized pixel art with a fixed light from the top left baked into the bevel colours; roughness and height are values per drawn class, and the normal map treats each art pixel as a flat facet. Bricks are rectangles cut at whole art pixels; there are no corner pieces, arches or openings. Courses are limited to a quarter of the art size so every brick keeps a face pixel. Output sizes that are not a whole multiple of art_pixels give art pixels of unequal widths. Occlusion is a blurred-height estimate posterized to eighths.
technique_references: Course and joint layout at whole art pixels with wrap-around
Bevel shading with highlight and shadow rows for a top-left light
Posterized fractal noise with ordered dithering for stone grain
